narrative.overview:
The first viewport is a night table with one warm lamp over it, and on it a sealed foil booster pack printed with the page's h1 (the name) and the title. The visitor rips it open. Twelve collectible cards, one per resume section, rise out of the pack and are flicked through one at a time. Then the spectacle stops. Everything below the pack is a calm, scannable landing page on the same plum-black ground. It sells in a fixed order: who he has shipped for, the highlights, the experience, one plain ask, about, skills, the full set, and a closing Contact band. On that page the colour comes from the card art and the six type colours. The chrome stays dark and quiet, and one lamp-amber accent marks every action.

There are two registers. The pack and the reveal are violent, glossy and physical: foil, crinkle, light, shards and haptics. The page under them is editorial and restrained: rows, rules, tags and quotes. The cards join the two registers, because the same card face appears in the reveal, in the set row, in inspect and in the Contact band. All content is real HTML and is server-rendered under the pack, so the page is complete without WebGL, without JavaScript motion, and on paper.

The world refuses the one-page scroll of hero, about, timeline and contact. It also refuses synthwave and neon, generic dark-neon glow, and any Pokémon trade dress (no yellow border, no logos, no names).
keyCharacteristics: A plum-black ground (never pure black) with a single warm lamp pool behind the pack.
One accent, lamp amber, used for every primary action, the focus ring and the selection.
Six card type colours carry all the hue below the fold, through card frames, row tints, tags and art borders.
Bricolage Grotesque, heavy and narrowed on its width axis, for every name and heading; Onest for everything you read.
A WebGL foil pack that tears for real, and a reveal where every card comes out face up except the secret rare.
Every card opens into inspect, which shows a big tilting card beside its full text.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Lamp amber is the only accent on the chrome. Each viewport has one primary Email me at most, plus the sticky one. No second accent appears.

rules.name: The Type Owns the Hue Rule
rules.body: Below the pack, saturated colour appears only through a card type: its art, its frame, its row tint and its tags. Nothing decorative gets a colour of its own.

rules.name: The Narrow Heavy Rule
rules.body: Display type is always weight 800 with `wdth` between 75 and 90. Bricolage is never set at its default width or a light weight.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Section titles stand alone. No uppercase eyebrows sit above them, and no line sits above a card name. Uppercase tracking belongs to the printed pack only.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Every highlight and spill is warm and comes from the lamp or from inside the pack. Cool light appears only as the violet and teal rim lights in WebGL.

dos: Do keep lamp amber as the one accent, on Email me, focus, selection and rarity notes only.
Do colour anything that belongs to a job through its card type (`--t` / `--frame`) and OKLab mixes of it.
Do size everything on a card in `cqw`, so one card face serves the reveal, the set row, inspect and the Contact band.
Do set display type in Bricolage 800 narrowed (`wdth` 80–90), and read-text in Onest.
Do keep every claim word for word from the approved resume copy. Highlight tiles are quotes, not paraphrases.
Do bring cards out face up. Only the secret rare arrives face down and turns.
Do keep the spectacle above the fold and the page below it calm, scannable and complete as HTML, with no WebGL, under reduced motion and in print.
Do keep one working Email me reachable at all times: hero, sticky header or dock, the ask and the band.
donts: Don't ever print the dog's name, in copy, alt text, labels or metadata. Call it a French bulldog.
Don't write corny copy. Use plain, direct, first-person wording close to the resume, with no puns, no game-speak and no hype.
Don't give an employer card a rarity. Only the player card is rare and only the Contact card is the secret rare.
Don't put a line, kicker or eyebrow above a card name or a section title.
Don't use Pokémon trade dress: no yellow border, logos or names.
Don't go synthwave, neon or generic dark-glow. The light is one warm lamp.
Don't add a second accent colour, or give a decorative element a hue of its own.
Don't use pure black for the ground or hard offset shadows anywhere.
Don't autoplay sound, or play any sound or vibration under reduced motion or when muted.
Don't show unverified metrics, degrees, testimonials or private details on a card or tile.
